title: Bulk Cu lattice constant optimization
action: Optimize the lattice constant of bulk fcc Cu using plane-wave DFT to obtain the equilibrium Cu lattice constant for constructing Cu(111) and Cu(100) slabs.
description: DFT optimization of bulk Cu to determine equilibrium lattice constant.

title: Optimize gas-phase glycerol and acetol molecules
action: Perform DFT geometry optimization of isolated glycerol and acetol molecules in a sufficiently large vacuum cell to obtain their total energies.
description: DFT optimization of isolated glycerol and acetol molecules.

title: Build and relax bare Cu(111) and Cu(100) slabs
action: Construct Cu(111) (4×4, 4 layers) and Cu(100) (3×3, 4 layers) slab models using the optimized lattice constant, fix the bottom two layers, and relax the top two layers with DFT to obtain bare surface total energies.
description: Construction and relaxation of Cu(111) and Cu(100) slab models.

title: Build and relax non-hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110) model
action: Construct the γ-Al₂O₃(110) slab (24 Al2O3 units) from the Digne et al. bulk structure, place a tetrahedral Cu₄ cluster on the surface, fix bottom atomic layers, and relax with DFT to obtain the total energy of the dry supported catalyst model.
description: Construction and relaxation of non-hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110) model.

title: Build and relax hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110) model
action: Add 4 water molecules (dissociatively adsorbed as OH groups, corresponding to 5.9 OH nm⁻²) near the Cu cluster on the relaxed non-hydroxylated model and relax the hydroxylated surface with DFT to obtain the total energy.
description: Construction and relaxation of hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110) model.

title: Compute adsorption energies and O–H cleavage barriers for glycerol and acetol
action: For each surface model (Cu(111), Cu(100), non-hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110), hydroxylated Cu₄/γ-Al₂O₃(110)), determine the most stable adsorption configurations of glycerol and acetol at Cu and Al sites using DFT geometry optimizations. For glycerol on Cu(111), Cu(100), and the hydroxylated model (both Cu and Al sites), locate transition states for the initial O–H bond cleavage (terminated and central O–H groups where applicable) using nudged elastic band and dimer methods. Record the raw total energies (in eV) of the bare surface, isolated gas-phase adsorbate, the adsorbed complex, and (for barriers) the initial state and transition state for each system.
description: Raw total energies from which binding energies and activation barriers are recomputed and compared to reference values.
output_schema: A JSON object with a 'systems' array. Each element is an object with keys: 'id' (string, one of the required identifiers listed in the contract), 'E_surface', 'E_adsorbate_gas', 'E_complex', 'E_initial', 'E_TS', optional 'note'. Required identifiers: glycerol_Cu111_BE, acetol_Cu111_BE, glycerol_Cu100_BE, acetol_Cu100_BE, glycerol_nonhydrox_Cu_site_BE, glycerol_nonhydrox_Al_site, acetol_nonhydrox_Cu_site_BE, acetol_nonhydrox_Al_site_BE, glycerol_hydrox_Cu_site_BE, glycerol_hydrox_Al_site_BE, acetol_hydrox_Cu_site_BE, acetol_hydrox_Al_site_BE, barrier_Cu111_terminated_OH, barrier_Cu111_central_OH, barrier_Cu100_terminated_OH, barrier_Cu100_central_OH, barrier_hydrox_Al_site, barrier_hydrox_Cu_site_terminated, barrier_hydrox_Cu_site_central. If a stable molecular adsorption complex cannot be found for glycerol on the non-hydroxylated Al site (glycerol_nonhydrox_Al_site), omit E_complex and include a note.
